findings.concrete fix: Update resumption logic to verify if the exact post-mutation state was achieved (or wrap the operation and history append in a robust state guard) so it can safely clear the pending state and resume instead of permanently crashing.
findings.problem: Crash recovery fails if a crash occurs after mutating the engine state (e.g., via run_manifest or review_phase) but before clearing the pending status. On resume, the controller strictly requires fingerprint(current) == pending['source_fingerprint'], which raises a ControllerError and permanently blocks the case.

findings.concrete fix: Pass the prompt via standard input (stdin_bytes) for Gemini, just as is done for Codex, and adjust the 'agy' invocation to read its input from standard input instead of argv.
findings.problem: For the Gemini provider, the role adapter passes the untrusted prompt (containing codebase documents and up to 128KB of text) directly on the command line via the '--print' argument. This leaks untrusted contents to system process lists and risks exceeding Linux MAX_ARG_STRLEN limits.

result.reason: Implementation fails to recover safely from crashes during phase application and leaks untrusted inputs via command line arguments.
